{{Quote|Medically, she is completely healthy. For reasons we can't explain, we are losing her.|A Kallidahin-owned [[GH-7 medical analysis unit|GH-7 medical droid]] |<ref name="v_film">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]'', {{Film|III}}</ref>}}
The '''Kallidahin''', also known as '''Polis Massans''', were a race of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] cetaceans native to the world of [[Kallidah/Legends|Kallidah]], having obtained their misleading name due to their extensive century-spanning digs on their adopted home in [[Polis Massa/Legends|Polis Massa]]. The Kallidahin lacked facial features and were commonly mute, resorting to signs and telepathy to communicate. Though they had little contact with other species and were considered hermetic, they were known for their extraordinary medical, archaeological and xenobiological skills, and were regarded as compassionate beings who understood the value of life. They were also known for their massive xenobiology database.

Members of this species were mainly concerned with their excavation in Polis Massa, where they were secretly trying to find proof of any relationship between their own species and the original inhabitants of Polis Massa, the extinct [[Eellayin/Legends|Eellayin]]. Although they did little to contact the wider galaxy beyond their business with the similarly secretive [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]], they were kind to any visitors. The Kallidahin helped [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] several times, including trying to save the life of their ally [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] and taking care of the last stages of her pregnancy. In later years, the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] built an outpost in Polis Massa that was eventually raided by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], but the locals were unmolested during this time.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|I was just on my way to summon Osh Scal. He's our Polis Massan supply officer&mdash;the Inquisitor wants to question him since he's one of the few Polis Massans able to speak.|[[Maneeli Tuun/Legends|Maneeli Tuun]], of the minority Kallidahin with voice|<ref name="l2" />}}
[[File:Polis-Massan_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A pair of Kalladahins]]
The average Kallidahin was a short, thin being<ref name="na">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> unable to walk as fast as a [[Human/Legends|Human]] would or, on average, to compare to a Human's strength.<ref name="enh" /> They had skinny<ref name="de">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}</ref> bodies covered by soft<ref name="enh" /> gray skin<ref name="negas_enh" /> that, being thick, smooth, and partially insulating, pointed to their aquatic, cetacean ancestors. Their fibrous figures were also surrounded by anatomical features known as growth rings. During the [[Old Republic era]], xenobiologists could not identify the evolutionary reason that the species developed this tree-like trait.<ref name="na" />

The head was connected with the body through a long, thin neck.<ref name="v_film" /> A member of the species had a flat, pale<ref name="negas_enh" /> face, covered by an osmotic membrane<ref name="na_nd">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> that left them featureless.<ref name="de_enh_i9">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}, {{InsiderCite|90|Aliens of Episode III}}</ref> The only facial feature was a pair of black eyes.<ref name="enh_i9">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}, {{InsiderCite|90|Aliens of Episode III}}</ref> Those visual organs lacked any expressiveness,<ref name="nd">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> but they were deep-focus and useful for work deep underground and for research in the field of medicine. A member of this species also had thin arms<ref name="na" /> with nimble<ref name="enh" /> gray hands, each with four long, dexterous fingers including an opposable thumb.<ref name="negas_enh" />

Most<ref name="l2" /> Kallidahin were mute due to a natural lack of vocal cords.<ref name="negas_enh" /> Their language, known as [[Massan]], combined computers,<ref name="enh" /> sign language,<ref name="enh_i9_na">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}, {{InsiderCite|90|Aliens of Episode III}}, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> and the use of their mildly<ref name="na" /> [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] brains.<ref name="negas_enh" /> Their telepathy is a biological force ability, with even non-force sensitive Kallidahin being capable of utilizing telepathy. <ref name="enh_i9" /> The Massan language has been described as falling beyond the Human auditive spectrum when used in its purest form.<ref name="nd" /> However, a small subset of Kallidahin, referred to as "[[Kallidahin speaker|speakers]]" by their people, did possess vocal cords and could physically speak languages<ref name="Strongholds" /> such as [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]],<ref name="l2" /> though their voices were soft and strangely resonant.<ref name="Strongholds" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|There are certain tests we do on newborns. Of course we erased all the records and the memory of the droids, but we didn't erase all supply records. When our stocks are low, we do refill orders.|[[Maneeli Tuun/Legends|Maneeli Tuun]]|<ref name="l2" />}}
The Kallidahin were known for their compassion and kindness,<ref name="negas_enh" /> while their also characteristic discretion was not as widely known.<ref name="v">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> They greatly valued freedom and life in any form<ref name="na" /> and had such a peaceful nature and respect for life that only rarely would they follow a soldier's career. Although able to protect themselves and their culture when the need arose,<ref name="enh" /> they were not an aggressive species and rejected direct confrontations even when the greater goals of the species were at risk.<ref name="de" />

They felt an overwhelming desire to gain data about other species,<ref name="na" /><ref name="de" /> as they were analytical and felt the research was particularly important when related to the origins of their own species.<ref name="enh" /> They were gifted [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]] but, being unskilled in diplomacy, preferred study from afar instead of direct interaction with the beings of interest.

The species also had galaxy-wide fame for their skill in the fields of archaeology<ref name="g" /> and medicine.<ref name="enh_g">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}, [[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide|''Clone Wars Campaign Guide'']]</ref> Their medics, while not as abundant as their excavators, were known for being dedicated healers.<ref name="mini">{{SWMiniCite|set=Revenge of the Sith|pack=Polis Massa Medic}}</ref> Many members of the species were miners or speleologists, and wore form-fitting bodysuits fitted with all manner of signaling devices, medical equipment and utility pouches.<ref name="negas_enh" /> The majority of these miners were seasoned spelunkers, and dug deep into the core of the asteroid field of Polis Massa to locate prize artifacts. All of them were committed and enthusiastic workers who commonly enjoyed a full day of work in the core of the asteroid field.<ref name="na" />

==History==
===Origins===
[[File:Polismassans.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Two Kallidahin]]
{{Quote|Oobah, oobah.|Recorded utterance in Kallidahin-designed [[Chroon-Tan B-Machine/Legends|midwife droid]]|<ref name="na_nd" />}}
Although most of the galaxy believed the Kallidahin to be the original inhabitants of the planetoid [[Polis Massa/Legends|Polis Massa]], the species had actually evolved on a different world known as [[Kallidah/Legends|Kallidah]],<ref name="g" /> in the [[Subterrel sector/Legends|Subterrel sector]].<ref name="de_enh_g_na_nd">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}, [[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide|''Clone Wars Campaign Guide'']], ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

The planet Polis Massa, in the more isolated limits of<ref name="na" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="dp_enh_g">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}, [[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide|''Clone Wars Campaign Guide'']]</ref> was instead the original home of a subterranean<ref name="dp">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}</ref> civilization known as the [[Eellayin/Legends|Eellayin]]<ref name="enh_g" /> Many centuries before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Polis Massa exploded due to a natural disaster<ref name="de_g_na">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, [[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide|''Clone Wars Campaign Guide'']], ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> whose cause would remain unknown in further years.<ref name="de_enh_v">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}, ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The native Eellayin mysteriously<ref name="de_dp">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}</ref> vanished afterwards<ref name="dp_g">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, [[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide|''Clone Wars Campaign Guide'']]</ref> and the Kallidahin and the Republic subsequently considered the Eeyallin to be extinct.<ref name="enh" /> The planet became an asteroid field, with the biggest asteroid being renamed Polis Massa.<ref name="de_enh" />

Given Kallidahin reticence, few details were known of their past before the sixth century [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]].<ref name="na" /> At some point in the past, this species made a deal with another one to learn the cloning techniques<ref name="g_na_v">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]'', ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> from the secretive [[Cloning/Legends|clone]]-masters known as [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]]. The Kaminoans agreed to the deal in exchange for certain xenobiological data in the Kallidahin archives. Although the Kallidahin were not as adept as Kaminoans, they managed to employ the cloning technology sufficiently to re-build biological matter they had found in archaeological digs.<ref name="de" /> They believed themselves to be descendants of the ancient Eellayin species once native to [[Polis Massa/Legends|Polis Massa]],<ref name="de_enh_g_na">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}},
[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide|''Clone Wars Campaign Guide'']], ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> although they kept this conviction in secret.<ref name="enh_g_na_nd">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}, ''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]'', ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> The Kallidahin also learned to use cloning for medical purposes, although they were not as advanced as the Kaminoans in this field.<ref name="na" />

Later, in the sixth century BBY, the [[Archaeological Research Council/Legends|Archaeological Research Council]] decided to establish a [[Polis Massa Research Base|Research Base]] on the largest of the asteroid remnants of the [[Polis Massa system/Legends|Polis Massa system]], by then known as Polis Massa, to unearth evidence of this evolutionary link.<ref name="cl">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref>

Circa [[519 BBY/Legends|519 BBY]],<ref name="de_dp_nd">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> the entire population of Kallidah<ref name="na" /> left their homeworld to mine at Polis Massa.<ref name="enh_i9" /> They traveled to the biggest asteroids in the system<ref name="enh" /> to start looking for clues.<ref name="g" /> The main objective of the species in successive years would be discovering their real connection with the Eellayin.<ref name="de" /> Although their civilization officially covered the whole asteroid field, only the biggest asteroids had a settled population. They organized their new life in Polis Massa, centered around an archaeological dig that would be surrounded by a mining colony.<ref name="g" /> As the asteroids lacked a natural atmosphere and the Kallidahin were [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]]-breathers, they resorted to airtight buildings.<ref name="de" /> They built their new capital, [[Polis Massa Research Base|Polis Massa Base]], and organized imports of food, water and machinery, even if the system had no real exports.<ref name="enh" /> They also built, in one of the closed habitats, a high-quality medical center mostly equipped for the physiological needs of Kallidahin patients.<ref name="dp_na_v">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

In later centuries, they found many artifacts and remains of the Eellayin,<ref name="enh" /> although real proofs of the relation, commonly coming from the depths of the Polis Massa asteroid, were scarce.<ref name="v" /> The species had trouble with treasure hunters wanting to plunder their digs,<ref name="dp_enh_na">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> and with the raising [[Pirate/Legends|piracy]] in the Outer Rim Territories.<ref name="dp_na">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> The inhabitants of Polis Massa were quiet in their work to avoid attracting any undesired attention<ref name="dp_enh">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}</ref> and refused to get involved with the rest of the galaxy,<ref name="de" /> but nevertheless they kept their politeness when dealing with aliens.<ref name="nd" />

When their initial research began to take dozens of decades, the Kallidahin chose to remain in Polis Massa and continue their task for as long as needed; soon, they had been away from Kallidah for so long that the species had no living memories of their own origin.<ref name="enh" /> At that point, aliens in the galaxy began calling the Kallidahin with the name of Polis Massans because they had been living in Polis Massa for centuries.<ref name="de_dp_na_vd">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The species humbly accepted their new name, feeling honored<ref name="na" /> and with no objection.<ref name="de" />

At some point during their research, the Kallidahin found the remains of [[Wiyentaah/Legends|Wiyentaah]], an Eellayin city, and built an installation over it, to carefully excavate the metropolis little by little. Because many of the unearthed artifacts were fragile, they were kept in secure, sterile rooms.<ref name="dp" />

Other cultures began to speculate about the real connection between the Kallidahin and the Eellayin, but the Kallidahin were silent in that respect. As the Kallidahin were always anxious to learn about xenobiology, many other species believed that their traditional drive was their real motivation.<ref name="na" /> They said they wanted to preserve the memory of the lost Eellayin,<ref name="negas_enh" /> but certain outsiders believed they really wanted to resurrect their ancestors<ref name="g_na">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]'', ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> using their cloning technology.<ref name="enh_g" /> The species now called Polis Massans had previously cloned extinct lifeforms in other places.<ref name="dp" /> Following this hypothesis, they had not succeeded in cloning Eellayin because they had not found adequate genetic material.<ref name="enh" />

[[File:ChroonTanBMachine-NEGTD.png|thumb|right|200px|Kallidahin-designed droid mimicking Kallidahin facial features]]
The Kallidahin also began building droids through a company known as [[Polis Massa Pria Assemblage]]. They mostly manufactured machines for their own use instead of exporting them, mainly [[Excavation droid/Legends|archaeological]] droids and [[Mining droid|miner]] droids; but they also needed help in skills beyond xenobiology, like obstetrics. Apparently to that end, they built the [[Chroon-Tan B-Machine/Legends|Chroon-Tan B-Machine]], which had a face inspired in the species'.<ref name="nd" />

Another alien who had had contact with the Kallidahin was [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], a renowned [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]]. Yoda had dealt with the Kallidahin [[Maneeli Tuun/Legends|Maneeli Tuun]], operational head of the medical center of Polis Massa and firm supporter of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="l2" />

===Order 66===
{{Quote|Into exile, I must go. Failed, I have.|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|<ref name="v_film" />}}
In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Yoda became a fugitive and, along with his ally [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]], went to Polis Massa looking for a haven.<ref name="dp_rotstodo">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] / [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novel]] {{1st}} / [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|comic]] / [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)|junior novel]] / [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|illustrated screenplay]]</ref> He had chosen this asteroid field partly because it was remote,<ref name="v" /> adequate to harbor him,<ref name="de" /> and partly because he knew he could count on Tuun.<ref name="l2" /> Yoda was soon joined by his allies Jedi Master [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], droids [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and pregnant, injured Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], all of them traveling in Amidala's [[J-type star skiff|star skiff]].<ref name="dp_na_rotstodo">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] / [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novel]] {{1st}} / [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|comic]] / [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)|junior novel]] / [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|illustrated screenplay]]</ref> They asked the Kallidahin to help during the childbirth.<ref name="v" />

However, the available obstetricians were mostly members of an archaeological dig team,<ref name="i9">{{InsiderCite|90|Aliens of Episode III}}</ref> with only two of them being seasoned physicians; the others were exobiologists. Amidala's condition was so severe that they had no time to look for more prepared doctors. The doctors even had to operate in their mining bodysuits, not having a minute to change clothes. The Kallidahin who treated her were Maneeli Tuun, [[Dznori Xam/Legends|Dznori Xam]] and [[Selif Xam/Legends|Selif Xam]], with the added presence of [[Osh Scal/Legends|Osh Scal]],<ref name="v" /> a non-medic supply officer.<ref name="l2" />

Recognizing their unfamiliarity with Human parturition, the Kallidahin consulted their databank and resorted to a [[Chiewab Amalgamated Pharmaceuticals Company|Chiewab Amalgamated]]<ref name="nd" /> [[GH-7 medical analysis unit|GH-7 medical diagnosis droid]], an advanced droid<ref name="v" /> of which they had several units, to deal with Amidala's injuries; and a seldom-used<ref name="nd" /> Chroon-Tan B-Machine to help with the childbearing.<ref name="v" />

[[File:PolisMassaMedCenter-ROTS.png|thumb|left|250px|Kallidahin treating [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]]]

Although Amidala had twins, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]], she had lost any will to live and slowly refused to recover.<ref name="de_dp_na_nd_rotstodo">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]'', [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] / [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novel]] {{1st}} / [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|comic]] / [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)|junior novel]] / [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|illustrated screenplay]]</ref> The Kallidahins<ref name="v" /> and the droid<ref name="nd" /> did everything in their power to save her life, but failed.<ref name="rotstodo">{{Film|III}} / [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novel]] {{1st}} / [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|comic]] / [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)|junior novel]] / [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|illustrated screenplay]]</ref> R2-D2 secretly recorded all the events with his holocam.<ref name="dn3">''[[Dark Nest III: The Swarm War]]''</ref>

To keep the births a secret, the Jedi decided to simulate that Amidala was still pregnant when she had died.<ref name="rotstodo" /> The discreet Kallidahin agreed to keep the secret,<ref name="na" /> even if they probably did not understand the galaxy-wide importance of it.<ref name="nd" /> Kenobi and Yoda asked them to erase any record of the births, including a memory wipe of the used medical droids. However, the doctors had performed safety tests to the newborns, consuming several supplies, and the supply record was forgotten during the deletion.<ref name="l2" /> The Jedi and Organa left soon afterwards,<ref name="nd" /> heading to Naboo to bury Amidala.<ref name="rotstodo" />

===The Imperial Inquisition===
{{Quote|Now I must ask you something else. I'm afraid that Malorum is looking into Polis Massa. It's best if you don't know why. I managed to deflect the inquiry for a time, but I don't know what Malorum knows or what he's planning to do next. The answers to those questions can endanger every Jedi &mdash; and the fledgling resistance.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], to [[Ferus Olin]]|<ref name="l2" />}}
Soon afterwards, the by-then [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine set up the [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]], formed by special [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Intelligence]] agents,<ref name="l1">''[[The Last of the Jedi: The Desperate Mission]]''</ref> including an Inquisitor [[Malorum]]<ref name="l4">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Death on Naboo]]''</ref> in charge of the planet [[Bellassa/Legends|Bellassa]]. A source informed Malorum about the burial of Amidala, telling him that a Jedi had taken the corpse from Polis Massa to Naboo. Malorum wanted to discover more details about this to use the information against his rival [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] &mdash; secretly the father of Amidala's children.<ref name="l1" />

Malorum hired [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], a teenaged [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], to examine the medical records of the Polis Massa clinic and also Naboo.<ref name="l1" /> Never giving his own name, Fett visited Polis Massa as an Imperial investigator, copied all the files and took them to Malorum. Thanks to the precautions taken after the birth, those documents were useless to Malorum.<ref name="l2" />

Meanwhile, Obi-Wan Kenobi joined forces with former [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] learner [[Ferus Olin]] against Malorum, particularly when Kenobi discovered Malorum's interest in Polis Massa.<ref name="l1" />

Malorum dispatched a new agent, an Inquisitor by the name of [[Sancor]], who was an expert in record security.<ref name="l2" /> The personal interest of the Inquisitorius might have led the Kallidahin to suspect that the birth was more important than they had previously thought.<ref name="nd" /> Sancor dealt with Tuun and searched the memory banks of the medical droids. Sancor later asked Tuun for the supply records and the presence of supply officer Osh Scal. As Scal was among the few members of this species who had an audible voice, Sancor could question him personally.<ref name="l2" />

Obi-Wan Kenobi, following his instincts, split up from Olin to visit Polis Massa. Kenobi intercepted Tuun before the Inquisitor could find Scal and the Jedi asked Scal to forge the records Sancor was analyzing, giving him a more important, although fictional, fugitive to track. Kenobi also disguised himself as a Kallidahin and met with Sancor, pretending to be Scal; during the questioning, Kenobi tried to misdirect the Inquisitor.<ref name="l2" />

However, Sancor saw a graphic depiction of the real Scal in the records and noticed that Kenobi did not look like him. Sancor attacked Kenobi and Tuun, but Kenobi scared him by activating his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. Sancor tried to escape from the system to report to Malorum. Kenobi and him struggled, and Sancor was killed.<ref name="l2" /> In order to cover Kenobi's tracks, Tuun then sent a message to Malorum, describing the "accidental" death of his envoy who fell from an observation platform and landed on sharp chirurgical tools.<ref name="l4" />

[[File:Montajepandilla.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Kallidahin, left to right: [[Osh Scal/Legends|Osh Scal]], [[Maneeli Tuun/Legends|Maneeli Tuun]], [[Dznori Xam/Legends|Dznori Xam]], [[Selif Xam/Legends|Selif Xam]]]]

Kenobi had to leave the asteroid soon afterwards. He met with Olin and asked him to take care of Malorum. Kenobi specifically asked Olin to not allow Malorum to discover whatever had happened in Polis Massa.<ref name="l2" />

Malorum met with Darth Vader soon afterwards and mentioned that he was researching events in the planetoid Polis Massa. Darth Vader forcefully requested Malorum to forget any work in that direction. Olin, who was secretly eavesdropping on the conversation, was sure that Malorum would continue probing Polis Massa.<ref name="l3">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Underworld]]''</ref>

Malorum personally visited Polis Massa soon after this event; however, even he was unable to find anything there. He then tried his luck on Naboo and discovered useful information. Malorum was then found by Olin and died while dueling him; the truth about the birth in Polis Massa remained a secret.<ref name="l4" />

===Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|By the time of the raid in Polis Massa, the men of the 501st were starting to get sick of the so-called Rebellion. These Rebels were different. They were organized, they were growing and they were everywhere.|Diary of the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st]]|<ref name="BF2">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref>}}
{{Main|Raid on Polis Massa}}

The Polis Massans opposed the Galactic Empire from its earliest days, but their remote location, limited contact with the wider galaxy, and focus on archaeological research kept them largely outside Imperial attention. Their combination of political disapproval and geographic isolation made the Polis Massa asteroid a suitable site for a concealed Rebel presence.<ref name="Strongholds" />

During the first days of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], a movement that started in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], the Rebel command mounted a secret base on Polis Massa. The Alliance launched several operations from this base, although the crew did their best not to disturb the nearby excavations.<ref name="na" />

The Empire raided this base repeatedly without achieving its destruction; during all these conflicts, the digs of the Kallidahin were untouched.<ref name="na" /> In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], when Darth Vader sent his elite [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] to recover important information that the Rebels had stolen, the Empire annihilated the base and killed all the Rebels, again without disturbing the nearby Kallidahin.<ref name="BF2" />

===Later conflicts===
{{Quote|Master, can you change what you saw in the holo?''"<br />"''Of course not.''"<br />"''That's right. You can only accept it. Some misfortunes you can prevent, and you will. But others&hellip; sometimes all you can do is embrace the pain.|[[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] after watching a recording of Kallidahin and [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]|<ref name="dn3" />}}
During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] ([[25 ABY/Legends|25]]&ndash;[[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]]), the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] invaders found no reason to raid Polis Massa: it was too remote and held no strategic value or important resources that they could use.<ref name="na" /> The later [[Dark Nest Crisis]] of [[36 ABY]] was similarly clement with the Kallidahin. During this campaign, however, R2-D2 showed his holorecording of Polis Massa to by-then adult Luke Skywalker, his wife [[Mara Jade Skywalker]] and his nephew [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]], along with other files of Padmé Amidala's later days. By then, Jade was suspected to have murdered her husband's mother, and the droid's files served to clear her name.<ref name="dn3" />

==Kallidahin in the galaxy==
Perceived by others as silent and weird,<ref name="dp" /> Kallidahin were considered among the most mysterious species in the galaxy.<ref name="i9_nd">{{InsiderCite|90|Aliens of Episode III}}, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> The mute, faceless sentients were not social creatures in the way Humans could be.<ref name="na" /> They limited their contact with other species<ref name="i9_na">{{InsiderCite|90|Aliens of Episode III}}, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> as a way to protect their work.<ref name="enh_v">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}, ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The Kallidahin had a massive database with xenobiological information about many alien species, but nevertheless they had little face-to-face contact with other cultures.<ref name="de" /> Probably the most exhaustive contact the Kallidahin had with another species was with the Eellayin, an extinct people whose memory they tried to preserve in their digs.<ref name="dp enh g i9 na nd">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CWenhancement1|text=''The Clone Wars'' Web Enhancement 1: Polis Massan}}, [[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide|''Clone Wars Campaign Guide'']], {{InsiderCite|90|Aliens of Episode III}}, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

The Kallidahin, commonly restricted to the Polis Massa system, rarely encountered any other sentients beyond the pirates<ref name="dp_na" /> and treasure hunters who wanted to profit from the locals' hard work.<ref name="dp_enh_na" /> The Kallidahin had dealt with the similarly reclusive Kaminoans in the past, obtaining important technology in exchange for their data on xenobiology,<ref name="de_g_na_v">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, [[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide|''Clone Wars Campaign Guide'']], ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> but the Polis Massans would rather be secretive about the results of their work.<ref name="dp_enh" />

Sometimes, the Kallidahin went beyond the borders of the Polis Massa system, commonly for exobiological reasons, but in those cases they did not go too far. Soon before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], some exobiologists of this species were sent to a different planet in the Subterrel sector to perform research. The local fauna included fierce predators, but the exobiologists managed to keep them at bay using [[Mk I Saberdart/Legends|Kamino saberdarts]] they had obtain in their deals with the Kaminoans. Another traveler to the planet, a [[Besalisk/Legends|Besalisk]] known as [[Dexter Jettster/Legends|Dexter Jettster]], witnessed the use of the saberdarts and was impressed with them.<ref name="v" />

Although their personality and telepathic abilities could have given them excellent careers in the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], or in certain criminal activities, there were no known precedents of Kallidahin Jedi or rogues.<ref name="enh" />

Some Kallidahin, including Maneeli Tuun, supported the Galactic Republic following their firm beliefs, but they remained mostly beyond the reach of the Republic's judicial arm. Jedi Master Yoda, and later Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi, were known to have trusted this cetacean of firm ideals.<ref name="l2" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Polegomassa.jpg|thumb|left|220px|A Kallidahin with babies [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] as seen in the [[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga|''LEGO Star Wars'']] video game]]
{{Quote|For a while, we weren't sure if the face design was supposed to be a mask, but George eventually made it clear that it ''was'' the face and that there were no markings or other features than the eyes. It would be skin.|[[Robert E. Barnes]], concept sculptor for the Prequel Trilogy|<ref name="de_enh_i9" />}}
The Polis Massans first appeared in the [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] ([[2005]]), and then in the movie and most of the adaptations ([[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)|junior novel]], [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|illustrated screenplay]], [[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga|''LEGO'' video game]]). They are notably absent in the [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|comic-book]] adaptation, in which Padmé Amidala is operated on only by droids. Conversely, in the video game ''LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga'', Amidala is treated only by a Kallidahin, with no visible droids.

The first conceptual art for these beings was drawn by illustrator [[Doug Chiang]] for [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="de_i9">{{DB|species|polismassan|Polis Massan}}, {{InsiderCite|90|Aliens of Episode III}}</ref> Following concept sculptor [[Robert E. Barnes]]'s memories of the event, director [[George Lucas]] provided Chiang with a monochrome photograph of a mask without any facial features except circled eyes.<ref name="i9" /> This appearance was considered for the Kaminoan species, but ultimately the design was rejected in favor of another that was considered more elegant.<ref name="de" />

Chiang's design went unused in ''Attack of the Clones''; however, it was later recovered for the following movie. After other early sketches for the species had been drawn by [[Stian Dahlslett]] and [[Sang Jun Lee]], an approximate idea for the species' outline was reached.<ref name="i9" /> [[Michael Murnane|Michael Patrick Murnane]] perfected Chiang's original designs<ref name="de" /> and then sculpted busts of the faceless aliens; when the statues received Lucas's approval, Murnane and Jun worked together on a full-body model. Murnane compared the result to creatures in [[Wikipedia:Hayao Miyazaki|Hayao Miyazaki's]] animated movie [[Wikipedia:Princess Mononoke|''Princess Mononoke'']].<ref name="i9" /> For the skin, a dolphin-like texture was used.<ref name="de" /> Finally, the movie featured computer-generated Polis Massans (the name "Kallidahin" had not been assigned yet) in a scene with a computer-generated medical droid.<ref name="de_i9" />

The novel ''[[The Last of the Jedi: Dark Warning]]'' (2005), by [[Jude Watson]], described Kallidahin Maneeli Tuun as particularly expressive for someone who lacked facial features as seen in the movie. In chapter 9, Tuun "looked thin and worried&hellip; a look of startled pleasure came over his face but then was replaced by the same frown." Later, his "troubled expression cleared," he "ran his hands along his cheeks and blew out a tired breath," and he even "gave a small smile." It is unclear how he can frown, blow out or smile without a brow or a mouth, as the descriptions are apparently not metaphorical.

===Non-canon content===
The following section describes the appearance of Kallidahin in official, albeit non-[[canon]]ical, stories. The non-canonicity of the story ''[[Old Wounds]]'', published in ''[[Star Wars: Visionaries]]'' (2005), is discussed in its own article and [[Darth Maul/Legends#Hunting Obi-Wan|the "behind the scenes" section of Darth Maul's]], as several other sources seem to reference it, but the whole story was confirmed as non-canon by [[Leland Chee]] soon after its publication.<ref name="chee">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=125719&start=0675#10095628|thread=Event Timeline and Character Age Discussion|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2005-03-29|time=11:02 AM}}</ref>

The plot followed [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] after having been defeated by Obi-Wan Kenobi on Naboo in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. Through unexplained means, Maul had survived and became a cyborg, and in [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]] Maul was tracking Kenobi, driven by revenge. Maul followed Kenobi's trail from Mustafar to Polis Massa, where he killed at least two mute Kallidahin in what he deemed an unsatisfactory carnage. Later, Maul checked his victims' medlog and somehow learned that Kenobi was on Tatooine. Maul then left Polis Massa and continued with his chase.<ref name="OW">{{StoryCite|story=Old Wounds|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref>
